newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mostly lower, soyoil posts gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mostly lower, soyoil posts gains.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended mostly lower on Friday while soyoil closed up on unwinding of spreads and on fund and commercial buying, traders said.
Some floor sources noted speculation of soyoil business in the works as commercials were active buyers and cash basis levels firmed.
Cash soyoil brokers on Friday quoted basis levels at 0.75 cent per lb under May CBOT futures, versus 1.35 under the May on Wednesday.
Pit sources said ADM, Cargill Inc, Continental Grain and Term Commodities were all buyers of soyoil in morning trade.
Funds bought at least 2,000 lots of soyoil on the day but were strong sellers of soymeal. Chartists pointed to a technical buy signal in the July soyoil.

Traders said soymeal found early support from Thursday's National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush report which showed U.S. weekly soybean crushings at 26.2 million bushels, near the high end of expectations.
But gains were capped by news stevedores at Brazil's Paranagua Port did not join a national strike.
Soymeal closed $0.90 per ton lower to $0.70 higher while soyoil ended 0.32 to 0.10 cent per lb higher.

On the day, funds bought at least 2,000 lots soyoil. Lee B. Stern bought 500 July, Smith Barney bought 400 July and 100 May, Iowa Grain bought 500 July and Griffin Trading bought 200 May, pit sources said.
In soymeal, Smith Barney sold at least 500 lots July and Prudential Securities and R.J. O'Brien each sold 200 May.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 21,848 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 21,000 lots, against Thursday's 15,285.
